### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-email`, `@objectstack/downstream-contract`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1959aacd1572fc8e403f8bd9c0ddbfe981321351`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **13** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-defaults/system.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/system.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **140** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1959aacd1572fc8e403f8bd9c0ddbfe981321351` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `31ef4a31a254366458dafed20f364bfeb0192269` — the merge of head `1406d0ee78d3bcab5649fc11c7dcfc83ef6b4c50` into base `1959aacd1572fc8e403f8bd9c0ddbfe981321351`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 31ef4a31a254366458dafed20f364bfeb0192269 && git checkout 31ef4a31a254366458dafed20f364bfeb0192269
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1959aacd1572fc8e403f8bd9c0ddbfe981321351 1406d0ee78d3bcab5649fc11c7dcfc83ef6b4c50 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1959aacd1572fc8e403f8bd9c0ddbfe981321351 && git merge --no-ff 1406d0ee78d3bcab5649fc11c7dcfc83ef6b4c50

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1959aacd1572fc8e403f8bd9c0ddbfe981321351
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1959aacd1572fc8e403f8bd9c0ddbfe981321351` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1406d0ee78d3bcab5649fc11c7dcfc83ef6b4c50`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed at 2026-10-12T14:38Z by an isolated subagent of `domain:spec` seat 1 (seat post #6017), session `session_019G5ZnRrTMiwcHG6iZM19zf`. Inputs: card #22876 (body and all 14 comments, the two `os-dev-report`s, the seat's orders and its merge-round acceptance `6126229625`), PR #22990 (body, 40-file list, net diff against `main` at `4267484fe`), the 48 check-runs on this head, and cards #22994 / #23001 with PRs #23024 / #23023 only as far as the safety claim leans on them. Nothing was built, run or re-run; the repository reads below are `git show` / `git grep` against this head and against the sibling at the pin this head names.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept set, `EmailTemplateDefinitionSchema` (the `email_template` type, a `strictObject`):

- `category` (enum, default `custom`) and `isSystem` (boolean, default `false`) go from accepted-with-default to refused at every value through `retiredKey()` — **right**: the playbook's route for a strict shape (the `tsc` channel plus the prescription at parse, instead of a bare unknown-key verdict). The pin refuses every former value, both old defaults, a foreign type, both keys at once, and holds at the registry binding (`getMetadataTypeSchema('email_template')` is the same object), at `defineEmailTemplateDefinition`, at `defineStack` (`STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID`, 422, paths `emailTemplates[0].category` / `.isSystem`) and on the `tsc` channel (two `@ts-expect-error` lines in a file the repo project compiles; `TypeScript Type Check` green). The did-you-mean is pinned never to steer `categry` / `isSytem` onto a tombstone.
- Output narrowing: a parsed template no longer carries either key while the live defaults `locale` and `active` still materialize (the lint pin's control) — **right**, and it is exactly what clears the dead-property advisory the card names.
- The two prescriptions follow the five house conventions: the fully qualified key in backticks first, `was removed in @objectstack/spec 17 (ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove)` (the spelling 107 tombstones at this head use for the 17 line), a dash clause on why the key was inert, the imperative fix with what works instead, and the house `os migrate meta --from 17` sentence — **right** (`retired-key-migrate-sentence.test.ts` is in the green repo project).

Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/system`:

- `EmailTemplateDefinitionCategorySchema` (const) and `EmailTemplateDefinitionCategory` (type) are removed — **right**: an orphan value schema whose only consumers were the key and the type-alias pin (`sys-email-template.object.ts` spells its own option list). The four ratchets move the way a whole-def deletion must: `api-surface` −2, `declaration-map` −2, `export-origins` −2, `json-schema.manifest` −1 (the manifest key deleted on purpose, the per-key ratchet's "def no longer emitted" path), `references/index.mdx` 1524 → 1523 and the page's enum section gone. `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR[18]` gains `system/EmailTemplateDefinitionCategory`, the file named per `entries/README.md`.
- Pinned sibling (AGENTS.md Post-Task 4): `Console Pin Gate` was skipped on this head by its paths filter, so I read the sibling at the pin the head names. `.objectui-sha` is objectui `9646e2ed2bf3` on this head and on `main`; at that commit `git grep EmailTemplateDefinitionCategory` returns nothing, and `default-schemas.ts` already drops the two fallback inputs (objectui#12193 merged as that commit). The removal breaks nothing pinned — **right**.
- `EmailTemplateDefinition` / `EmailTemplateDefinitionParsed` lose two keys (input typed as the retired mark, output absent): breaking for any reader of `template.category`; measured none in this repository (the loader's `toRenderInput` and the service reads carry neither), the D3 entry asks the author about readers of their own, and the BREAKING banner carries it — **right**.

Authorable-surface artifacts: two rows become `… [RETIRED]` and no row disappears (the tombstone route keeps the rows) — **right**; `authorable-defaults/system.json` drops the two defaults by hand — **right**, that ratchet does not record a removed default on its own.

ADR-0087 registration, three obligations:

- D2 `email-template-category-is-system-removed`: `toMajor: 18`, `retiredFromLoadPath: true`, `retiredAfter: '17.7.0'` (the package label at this head, which the census pin takes for an unpublished entry), `stripKeys` over `mapCollection(stack, 'emailTemplates')` — a lossless delete, idempotent by construction, one notice per key, the path naming the template; fixture with 4 notices (the built-in shape, the 17.x-emitted shape, a canonical control) — **right**. Placement: inserted by identifier between `elementTextVariantHeadingLevels` and `fieldColumnListsCanonicalized`, defined directly above the latter, `order: 62` is one more than the previous highest (61) and unique — **right** per the list's own header (`conversions-major18-merge.test.ts` holds both rules; green).
- `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]`: `system/EmailTemplateDefinition:category` and `:isSystem`, one entry file each, named per the README; the pin asserts no other major carries an `EmailTemplateDefinition:` key — **right**.
- D3 `email-template-category-is-system-retired`: one family entry, `surface` backtick-free, `reason` names the D2 id, `acceptanceCriteria` non-empty; its `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment carries the same id, sits where that id sorts, `order: 94` — shared with one other in-flight fragment after the merge, which the header permits — **right**.
- Changeset marker `adr-0087: registered` naming exactly the D2 and D3 ids, one marker — **right** (`Check Changeset` success twice on this head).

The seams the safety claim leans on (the dependence the brief names):

- Stored rows: `applyConversionsToStoredItem` forces `includeRetired: true` (`conversions/stored.ts`); the pin replays an `email_template` row carrying both 17.x defaults to a clean row the write door accepts — **right**.
- Built artifacts, door 1: `58f5c9099` (#23023) is an ancestor of this head (`merge-base --is-ancestor`, exit 0). It replays every retired, non-flip step-18 entry for a `18.0.0` floor; this entry is a retired, non-flip step-18 entry, so a `^18` artifact built before this PR boots with it replayed. A `^17` artifact is refused at the protocol-18 handshake by design, not this PR's concern — **right**.
- The registry copy, door 2: `4267484fe` (#23024) is an ancestor and is this PR's merge base; `AppPlugin` now registers the forward-converted copy of every collection, so the served list and the email loader's execution read see the converted template — **right**.
- The pin's own artifact leg: `ObjectStackDefinitionSchema` refuses the persisted shape before `applyConversions(…, { includeRetired: true })` and accepts it after, with a lit control (`categry` refused on both sides) so the reading is not a tautology — **right**.
- Bound, stated honestly in the changeset: the out-of-repo consumer population (cloud included) is NOT MEASURED.

Form and bundles: `email-template.form.ts` drops the select and the checkbox with a comment in place; the served form was measured with neither field — **right**. The four `metadata-forms.generated.ts` bundles lose `email_template.fields.category` / `.isSystem` and nothing else — **right** (`check:i18n` inside `Lint & Repo Gates`, green); the catalog count pin 670 → 668 is two labels in three locales — **right**.

Liveness ledger: both rows STAY `dead`, re-noted on the house REMOVED template (tombstoned at the schema; stripped by the protocol-18 conversion; the entry stays because `retiredKey` keeps the key in the walked shape, the `rls.priority` precedent; what to do instead), `_note` and the README row updated, the dead count unchanged so `state-counts` does not move — **right** (`Spec property liveness` success). Deleting the rows would have reported UNCLASSIFIED.

Writers inside the radius: the six built-in auth templates (12 lines), the showcase template, the ADR-0054 dogfood fixture, the downstream-contract fixture, two plugin-email test fixtures and three docs examples drop the keys; the typed ones were forced by `tsc` (the built-ins are typed `EmailTemplateDefinition`) — **right**. The tree-scoped absence walk reads five roots (`packages`, `examples`, `skills`, `content`, `scripts`), the per-extension set under `packages/`, the non-code extensions plus `examples/*/src/**/*.ts` under `examples/` — exactly the radius `scripts/cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` already declares for `@objectstack/spec` (the #15513 and #20126 pins hold those globs, `heldBy` witnesses present, `turbo.json`'s `@objectstack/spec#test:repo` mirrors them), so the playbook's declared-once-per-package rule is met without an edit (`check:cross-package-test-inputs` green). Its exclusions are structural, each with its reason, not an allowlist file: the pin itself, `packages/spec/src/conversions/` (the fixture must author the keys), `packages/spec/liveness/` (the rows classify the shape, and `category` sits beside the `bodyHtml` row there), `content/docs/releases/`, the gitignored `packages/spec/json-schema/`, and `CHANGELOG.md` — **right**. Bounds I name beyond the test's own list: `.tsx` and the whole `conversions/` directory are outside the walk (the typed channel covers the first; the second is spec-internal), as are `docs/**`, `.claude/**`, `.github/**` and the repo-root files. The matcher's anti-vacuity case and the visited-file floors make a silent empty walk fail.

Lint pins: `lint-liveness-properties.test.ts` pins that a parsed template lints clean and carries neither key, and that the parse refuses an authored one; `runtime-gate.inert-type-writes.test.ts` returns the `email_template` door to silent and asserts the door's schema refuses `category`; the showcase control is silent — **right**: the advisory left because the parse no longer emits `category`, which is the card's "advisory gone".

Docs and census: `automation/email-templates.mdx` (three examples, the `category` paragraph rewritten), `permissions/system-context.mdx` (the collision row now says tombstone), `scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs` (`NON_READ_ANCHORS` prose; the `isSystem` anchor still resolves because the tombstone keeps the property name) — **right**. `content/docs/references/**` regenerated (`check:docs` inside `TypeScript Type Check`, green). No `content/docs/releases/` page and no `CHANGELOG.md` is touched — **right**.

Scope and class: exactly the two seed keys; no other `dead` row, not `.objectui-sha`, not the `sys_email_template` object's own columns; the 40-path file list has zero hits in `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `docs/adr/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md` (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success); 1,283 changed lines, under 3,000; head repository equals base repository; draft, no auto-merge, not queued — **right**: a Tier S record is the right instrument and nothing in the class needs a human approval.

Merge-round deltas in the net diff: the type-alias pin resolved to 775 (main's `InstallModeSchema` +1 stacked with this −1, both history notes kept, the count recomputed from source by the test itself) — **right**; `references/index.mdx` and `package-api-assembled.mdx` regenerated from the merged tree — **right**; the runtime fixture is judged in ③.

Check-runs on this head as read: 48 runs — 41 success, 7 skipped, 0 failure, 0 in progress (the second `Check Changeset`, re-triggered by the body edit, finished success). The seven required contexts: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (all six shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` success; `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` skipped by its paths filter (no driver or temporal path in the diff), as are `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood shard matrix and the opt-in tarball smoke — by design, not red. `pnpm check:platform-checklist` (8 findings, identical on `main` `4267484fe`) is not a check-run on this head and names none of this diff's files.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/22876-email-template-category-is-system-retired.md`: `@objectstack/spec` **`minor`** with the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM → TO table (every `category` value, `isSystem` true and false, the enum import, the type), the one-line fix, both prescriptions quoted, and one `adr-0087: registered` marker — **matches the diff**: a refused authorable surface and a removed export are breaking; the house rule during the launch window is `minor` plus the banner (`check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`), and the banner is what `check-adr-0087-registration` reads breaking-ness from.
- `@objectstack/plugin-email` **`patch`**: the six built-ins drop two inert keys and render and send as before — **right**. `@objectstack/platform-objects` **`patch`**: the generated bundles drop two labels — **right**.
- Rightly undeclared: `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/runtime` (test files only), `@objectstack/dogfood`, `@objectstack/downstream-contract` and `@objectstack/example-showcase` (private), `scripts/**`, `content/docs/**`. No `skip-changeset` label — **right**.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body (line 2), in the claim `6117767270`, in the changeset body, and in triage's correction `6118067953` — consistent, and **right**: the diff widens no accept set and enlarges no public surface (two keys refused, one def removed, two defaults gone, two form inputs gone; the new conversion and registry entries are the retirement's own bookkeeping), and `(narrowing)` declares the breaking direction the way `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` defines it. Triage's first `yes (narrowing)` was wrong and is corrected on the card.

### ③ Boundary flags

Stage-0 report `6117722169`:

- `open_questions[0]`, the six `realtime_subscription` rows (A / B / C): the seat bounded the batch to the two seed keys (claim `6117767270`, option A) and the diff honours the bound — no other ledger row, no `skills/**`. That family's verdict is not in this PR and stays the human-floor decision its ledger file records; nothing to escalate from this record. **Answered: outside this PR, bound kept.**
- `out_of_scope_findings`: the objectui fallback `skill.triggerPhrases` — carried by the companion and landed (objectui#12193 is the pin); the unreachable `JobPreview` / `EmailTemplatePreview` reads — carrier none, noted; the future v18 `sys_email_template` promotion writer copying `category` / `is_system` into an item — a real forward hazard for whoever builds that writer, and a loud one: the write door now refuses both keys and `convertStoredItem` strips them at read; the stale realtime ledger note — carrier the realtime decision; `manifest.integrity` / `view.name` dead-with-readers — the ledger owner. **All answered as carried; none is this PR's.**

Build report `6120111318`:

- `open_questions[0]`, the retired-default residue stage (A / B / C): option **A stands and is right** — tombstones only, so the parse agrees with `tsc`; a residue stage would silently accept at parse what `tsc` refuses and would cover only the default values, not an authored `category: 'auth'`. The populations that carried the materialized defaults are healed at the seams: stored rows (`applyConversionsToStoredItem`, pinned here), built artifacts (door 1, `58f5c9099`), the registry copy (door 2, `4267484fe`), and the undeclared-engines artifact (converted at the metadata door, measured on #22994). Option C was measured (`6120481114`), found both doors, filed #22994 (door 1 split to #23001), both fixes landed and both are ancestors of this head. **Residue is not needed; adopting it now would hide for one type the class defect the doors fixed for every type.**
- `deviations`: the two count pins outside the claimed surface (`object-lifecycle-panel-echo-decisions.test.ts` 670 → 668 after #22943's +1 stacked; `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts` 776 → 775 after main's +1 stacked) — each moved only by what this retirement removes, declared in the body — **accepted**; residue not adopted — above; two merges through `os-regen-merge.sh`, sharded runs, background verdict reads, turbo type-check — measurement mechanics, not contract — **accepted**; `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/integration-system.json` left stale — a prose description, not an authoring, outside the surface and outside the walk — **Acceptance notes, carrier the next edit of that file**; the Studio door measured as `PUT /api/v1/meta/email_template/:name?mode=draft` (200 without the keys; 422 `INVALID_METADATA` with either key or both 17.x defaults) — **accepted**, it is the door Studio calls.
- `out_of_scope_findings`: `pnpm check:platform-checklist` exits 1 on `main` — pre-existing, not a per-PR check-run, carrier the watchdog — **not this diff's**; the objectui `registry.ts` docstring — the companion's acceptance notes; the compiled-artifact door hypothesis — measured and closed through #22994 / #23001.

Seat orders `6120180938`, `6120481114`, `6123939287`, `6124146159`: the park, the two `Blocked-by:` lines and the unlock are all discharged on this head — both doors are ancestors, the pin condition holds on the head and on `main`, the body carries no `Blocked-by:` line (read back).

Merge-round report `6126177600` and the seat's acceptance `6126229625`:

- Conflicts: the type-alias pin to 775 by the pin's own counter — **right**; the two generated reference pages regenerated from the merged tree, the deferral discharged — **right**. The dev's patch-id reading (35 of 40 files byte-identical before and after the merge) is the dev's measurement; what this record judged is the net diff itself.
- The fixture edit in `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin-converted-collections.test.ts` (door 2's own test, `domain:cli`): the fixture authored a 17.x-emitted template (`category: 'custom'`, `isSystem: false`), this PR's tree-scoped absence walk refused it on `c116f7607` (`Test Core (1/6)` red), and `1406d0ee7` drops the two keys from the literal and corrects the docstring and header, assertions unchanged, 8 of 8. **The leg it no longer exercises:** that file's email-template legs no longer prove that `AppPlugin`'s converted copy strips these two keys; they still prove list-versus-item parity and the loader's parse over a template with no retired key. **Judgment: the edit is right and the loss is accepted with its gap named.** The playbook forbids a kit exclusion in an absence pin (an absence assertion is not a stale mention; excluding the hit deletes the guard) and a non-literal spelling would evade the gate, so the only honest options were this edit or the red. The composition stays pinned in two halves: door 2's generic forward conversion by the same file's dashboard legs over a retired step-18 entry, and this entry's strip by this PR's conversion block (the stored seam, the artifact boot door before and after, every value shape, idempotence, retirement from the load path). The end-to-end reading of these two keys through `AppPlugin` was taken once at `c116f7607` (8 of 8 with both keys present) and recorded in the report — a measurement, not a standing pin. Carrier none, as the seat accepted; I concur. Not a FAIL condition: no gate loses coverage of the composition.
- `check:type-check-debt` ran although the order said NOT MEASURED — exit 0, harmless, corrected by the seat — **accepted**.
- `origin/main` has moved past the merge base (it read `e49aaec73` at this review); the dev reports none of those commits touch this diff's files and `mergeable_state` reads `clean`. The queue rebuilds on current `main`; the regenerated reference pages and the two count pins are the files to re-check if `main` moves them before the queue — the landing seat's pre-queue step, not a flag on the diff.
- The PR body handed as a file was applied by the seat: the `## Merge round (head 1406d0ee7)` section and the un-parked blockquote are on the body as read.

PR acceptance notes: bound kept — verified on the file list; the stale checklist prose — accepted; the #22874 / #22943 overlap merged in — the diff carries their lines; the out-of-repo population NOT MEASURED — stated in the changeset; the companion merged and the pin at or past it — verified on the head and on `main`.

The card's "Done when", against the diff and the measurements on the card: authoring refuses `category` and `isSystem` with the prescription (pinned at four doors, measured at the Studio door) — met; the ledger rows retire with them (re-noted tombstones, which is what "retire" means on the tombstone route) — met; the advisory on every template gone (the lint pins) — met; Studio saves an email template without either key (200 at the same door, the served form carries neither field) — met.

Escalations: none.
